questions.question: What kinds of managed sites does the manual describe?
questions.reference_answer: ACI (fiber/GPON) sites, ACW (copper/switch-based) sites, and a small set of dedicated GPON sites.

questions.question: Which manufacturers' equipment is used at the dedicated GPON sites?
questions.reference_answer: Nokia GPON OLT and ONT equipment with Openwifi-brand wireless access points.

questions.question: What equipment will I not find when troubleshooting a GPON site?
questions.reference_answer: A traditional network switch and a Ruckus-brand access point are not present.

questions.question: A resident at a GPON site reports a connectivity alert. Who should I contact, the resident or the property office?
questions.reference_answer: Contact the resident directly rather than the property management office.

questions.question: How do I find the phone number of a resident in a specific unit?
questions.reference_answer: Search the account system for the property, enter the unit number in the secondary address field, then open the account record.

questions.question: What two things should I try with the resident on the call before booking a technician?
questions.reference_answer: Confirm the equipment has power and ask the resident to power cycle it.

questions.question: How long should equipment stay unplugged during a power cycle at a resident's unit?
questions.reference_answer: Roughly thirty seconds.

questions.question: An access point is reported offline. What should I check first?
questions.reference_answer: Check the link status of the switchport the AP is connected to.

questions.question: For an offline AP, how should VLAN 100 be set on the port the AP plugs into?
questions.reference_answer: VLAN 100 must be present and untagged on the AP's switchport.

questions.question: The AP is still offline although all three checks pass. What next?
questions.reference_answer: Power cycle the AP, check it is not in a factory-reset or provisioning state, then treat it as a hardware failure and follow Section 6.

questions.question: How should VLAN 100 be configured on the IDF switch port that an in-unit switch connects to?
questions.reference_answer: VLAN 100 must be present and tagged on that port.

questions.question: How long can an in-unit switch take to finish rebooting?
questions.reference_answer: Sixty to ninety seconds on some models.

questions.question: What does IDF stand for?
questions.reference_answer: Intermediate Distribution Frame.

questions.question: When an IDF switch is offline, which switch's port do I check the link status on?
questions.reference_answer: The port on the MDF/Core switch that the IDF switch is connected to.

questions.question: At what point should an IDF outage be escalated instead of troubleshot further?
questions.reference_answer: When a power cycle and the checks do not restore service quickly and ten or more units are affected.

questions.question: Why should I spend less time troubleshooting an IDF switch than a single in-unit device?
questions.reference_answer: An IDF outage can affect many devices at once, so quick escalation is preferred.

questions.question: What steps do I follow in the systems when replacing an access point or switch?
questions.reference_answer: Delete the old record from the controller and monitoring platform, clear the event log entry, add the new device as a new record with its new MAC address.

questions.question: Can I just change the MAC address on the existing device record to the replacement's address?
questions.reference_answer: No. Editing the MAC in place breaks monitoring-platform tracking; create a new record.

questions.question: Where can I read the MAC address of the replacement unit?
questions.reference_answer: Usually on a label printed on the device.

questions.question: How long should a replaced device take to show online in the monitoring platform?
questions.reference_answer: Within a few minutes.

Which firmware version is approved for 8000-model switches?
What should I do with a switch that is running an unapproved firmware version?
questions.reference_answer: Flag it for a firmware update before marking it resolved; do not deploy it to a live site.

questions.question: How do I check which firmware a managed switch is running?
questions.reference_answer: Use the show-version command or its equivalent in the management interface.

questions.question: What response time does an Emergency dispatch ticket require?
questions.reference_answer: Within 2 hours, same day.

questions.question: When must a Priority dispatch ticket be responded to?
questions.reference_answer: First thing the following morning (next business day).

questions.question: Who should I contact before I create a technician dispatch ticket?
questions.reference_answer: On-site property staff or maintenance personnel.

questions.question: Which kinds of problems justify an Emergency priority?
questions.reference_answer: Outages of shared infrastructure or multiple residents, and safety-related equipment issues.

questions.question: How many affected units within what time window make a multi-unit outage event?
questions.reference_answer: 10 or more units within a 2-hour window.

questions.question: Who do I contact first when escalating to the equipment vendor?
questions.reference_answer: The primary on-call escalation contact for that vendor relationship.

questions.question: What do I do if neither on-call escalation contact can be reached?
questions.reference_answer: Open an escalation ticket directly with the vendor's support portal.

questions.question: What details should I collect before making an escalation call?
questions.reference_answer: Property name or site identifier, number of units affected and how it was counted, when it started, shared failure point, checklists attempted.

questions.question: For a circuit-level fault, should I phone the ISP straight away?
questions.reference_answer: No. Open a ticket through the ISP's express ticketing portal first, then follow up by phone.

questions.question: What signs suggest a circuit-level fault rather than an on-site equipment fault?
questions.reference_answer: Healthy internal links and VLANs while the uplink toward the ISP is down or flapping, or several properties on the same circuit affected.

questions.question: Why do I need an express ticket before phoning the ISP?
questions.reference_answer: The ticket number is generally required before the ISP will discuss the case.

questions.question: Do I need to email the property manager to replace three units at a property?
questions.reference_answer: No. Process it through the case management system.

questions.question: What does the case management system do automatically once a replacement is logged?
questions.reference_answer: It creates the shipping request and the technician dispatch ticket.

questions.question: A resident asks for a copy of their invoice. Who handles that?
questions.reference_answer: Refer the resident to their property manager.

questions.question: Where should an ISP-level billing dispute be sent?
questions.reference_answer: To the ISP's dedicated special billing team.

questions.question: What must I add to a case when handing it off to the next shift?
questions.reference_answer: A comment with the current date, plus a summary of the current status and the next required action.
